what_a_row_is: the works-with grid per TI family: ran, partial, built, ships, early, community, untried, with evidence

rows.note: What works with what, per TI family: the tools, operating systems and maker platforms engineers already use. Rendered as the works-with grid on site/portability.html by portability/render.py. A cell is [state, short note, evidence path or site page], optionally followed by a fourth element, an object with `changed` (one short line: what had to change to run it, e.g. "316-line layer, 0 app edits") and `files` (the repo path of the folder's "Take it with you" section: the files a reader copies). Three-field cells stay valid. States: ran (run on a board), partial (ran up to a step; shown as Could work, the note names the blocker), built (built, not run; shown as Should work), ships (vendor tested: the SDK release notes name the tool and version as tested; cited, not repeated here), early (vendor early access), community (a third-party port exists), untried, gap (nothing found, dated in the source) and na (does not apply) draw an empty cell, and a row of only empty cells is not drawn. A family missing from a row is empty too. Sources: data/toolchains/ (what TI ships, scanned 2026-10-14), docs/research/toolchain-support-2026-10-14.md (third-party support, read 2026-10-14), the per-board results and project pages for anything marked ran or built.

faq.q: Can I build TI's Bluetooth or Zigbee examples for the CC23xx and CC27xx with GCC?
faq.a: Not from the F3 SDK as shipped. Those examples have no GCC makefile, and the Bluetooth stack libraries ship only for TI Arm Clang and IAR, the Zigbee libraries only for TI Arm Clang. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The driver examples do build with GCC (144 of 144 on two boards); for radio apps use TI Arm Clang, or IAR for Bluetooth (portability/toolchains/gcc-f3/README.md).

faq.q: Why did only 5 of 10 MSPM0 driver apps run on the CC2340R5 unchanged?
faq.a: The other 5 put chip detail into calls that are meant to be portable: MSPM0 apps put a pin-mux index into the GPIO_setConfig flags, some call DriverLib directly, and UART is named UART2 on the CC2340R5's SDK. **Tag: Tool or docs.** Each needs a few app edits; the card for test X1 lists them (portability/README.md).

faq.q: Why do some low-power examples lose the debugger?
faq.a: Examples that enter STOP, STANDBY or SHUTDOWN turn off the part of the chip the debugger talks to, so the probe cannot reconnect until the board is reset or power-cycled. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The runner skips or resets them; 10 G3507 examples were counted as not run for this reason.

faq.q: Why does the Zigbee light answer slower after re-pairing?
faq.a: Not explained. Two hours after a re-pairing the same image answered in 3.5 to 7.0 s instead of 95 ms median, while the coordinator reported a weaker link; the signal strengths were seen but not saved for every run. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Radio environment).** One board, one network (cc2340r5/FAQ.md).

faq.q: Why is the CC35X1 ESPHome device not in Home Assistant?
faq.a: The test Wi-Fi network keeps its clients apart, so Home Assistant on the home network cannot reach it. On the board, the ESPHome API answered 20 of 20 commands from a client. **Tag: Setup or handling.**

faq.q: Does IAR or Keil build TI's projects for my chip?
faq.a: TI ships IAR projects for most MSPM0, CC23xx and CC27xx, MSPM33 and AM13 examples and Keil projects for most MSPM0 and MSPM33 examples; the Works with grid gives the counts. IAR's IDE is Windows only. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The counts come from scanning every example folder on 2026-10-14 (data/toolchains/claims.csv).

faq.q: What is the difference between TI ships it, built and ran?
faq.a: TI ships it means TI's SDK has a project or makefile for that compiler; nobody here has built it. Built means it compiled and linked here. Ran means it was flashed to the board and ran with no fault; Verified means the board's behavior also matched a reference, such as TI's own build of the same example.

faq.q: Will my own GCC work, or only the Zephyr SDK's?
faq.a: The build used GCC 12.2 from the Zephyr SDK, through three small scripts that give it the arm-none-eabi names TI's makefiles call. TI names Arm GNU 9-2019-q4 for MSPM0. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The scripts and logs are in portability/toolchains/gcc-mspm0.

faq.q: Can I trust ran with no fault as works?
faq.a: Not on its own. It means the example started and kept running without a crash; it does not prove the example did its job. That is why each card and milestone says how many were also checked for behavior (for GCC on the L1306, 24 of 87).

faq.q: Which computer and versions are these results from?
faq.a: Most runs used one Intel Mac on macOS 15.7, with CCStudio 21.0.1 (TI Arm Clang 5.1.1), SysConfig 1.26.3, MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07, F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 and Zephyr 4.4.2, unless a card says otherwise. The L1306 blink image also built on Ubuntu 24.04 and Apple Silicon; each image was flashed and verified on the board from the Intel Mac (docs/frl.md). No Windows host run is recorded.

faq.q: What does ported by changing the device in SysConfig mean?
faq.a: TI's SysConfig tool writes the pin and peripheral setup code from a .syscfg file. Changing the device line in that file and rebuilding is the smallest port there is. When the new chip lacks a pin or peripheral, SysConfig stops or drops the setting, and the card says which.
